heading: INT. SECRETARY'S OFFICE, NEW YORK INSURANCE COMPANY - NIGHT (1927)

units.text: INT. SECRETARY'S OFFICE, NEW YORK INSURANCE COMPANY - NIGHT (1927)
A cramped office after hours.
A single green-shaded lamp.
Filing cabinets crowd the walls like silent clerks.
On the desk, a bulky wax-cylinder dictating machine, horn pointed up.
MILLICENT HARGROVE, thirties, trim in a navy dress, hair pinned firm, sits very straight.
She winds the crank with a gloved hand and adjusts the horn.
Testing. Millicent Hargrove, Policy Division, March the ninth, nineteen twenty-seven. If this is heard, the ledger in the lower drawer is the true one.
units.name: MILLICENT

units.text: She stops the machine.
Presses a lever.
The cylinder spins back, crackling.
...the ledger in the lower drawer is the true one.
units.name: MILLICENT
paren: from the machine, thin and tinny

units.text: She nods, satisfied.
Then her eyes lift to the frosted glass of the door.
A shadow passes slowly.
She holds perfectly still.
The shadow stops.
The doorknob rattles.
Not yet. Not yet.
units.name: MILLICENT

units.text: She snatches the cylinder from the machine and wraps it in her scarf.
The knob turns again.
She slides the lower drawer open, drops the bundle inside, locks it, and pockets the key in her stocking.
The door opens a crack.
Lamplight catches the edge of a man's hat.
Millicent lifts her chin and smiles the brightest smile of her life.
Come in, do. I've only just finished.
units.name: MILLICENT
